title: The gateway-bff composite screen routes are not specified in the API source
source: Recovery Workbench API Specification v4; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
section: API Specification v4 servers and paths (131 paths, 141 operations); Arch v5 slides 30 and 34 (edge); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-19
description: API Specification v4 is one document for the whole module: one server (/api/recovery/v1), 131 paths and 141 operations, all of them service operations. It holds no BFF route and no composite screen response. Arch v5 slide 30 notes describe the edge composition (the browser calls /api/recovery/cases/{id}; gateway-bff checks the Redis session and the coarse permission, then calls rwb-case GET /v1/cases/{id} and rwb-source-data GET /v1/customers/{id} and /v1/accounts/{id} in parallel and merges the answers into the screen model), and DP-19 maps a screen to a gateway-bff composite route with H RWB-PLT-N001-CON, but neither source gives the path, the operation, the parameters or the response of a composite route. The gateway-bff document of v5 therefore carries no screen route; inventing one would put a contract in the set that no source states.
evidence: API Specification v4 line 12 to 14: one server url /api/recovery/v1, description 'Relative to the ACE service in each environment'; no path in the file starts with /bff, /screens or /screen. Arch v5 slide 30 notes name the composition, the merge step and the 1.2 s p95 budget against the 2 s target but give no contract. Template and Rules R5.5 DP-19: 'Screen, ace-web -> gateway-bff composite route, H RWB-PLT-N001-CON'.
proposed: Confirm the BFF composite route per screen (path, operation, merged response) in RWB-PLT-N001-CON and publish it as a second document of the edge set, or state that the BFF stays a pure pass-through router with no composite route in this release.

title: PLT owns five v4 operations but the split has no PLT service document
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 (sheet Endpoints); Recovery Workbench API Specification v4; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
section: Ownership Map Endpoints rows for the four feature-flag paths and POST /admin/workflows/smoke; Template and Rules R8.4 API Specification output
description: Microservice Ownership Map v1 gives PLT as the owner of five v4 operations: GET /feature-flags, GET /admin/feature-flags, POST /admin/feature-flags, PATCH /admin/feature-flags/{flagKey} (ASM-A6-api-2) and POST /admin/workflows/smoke (ASM-A6-api-5). Template and Rules R8.4 splits the API Specification into 19 files plus gateway-bff and an index, and PLT is not one of the 19 services, so no service document can hold them. The base path of these operations under the BFF is also unstated: v4 uses the single base /api/recovery/v1, and the per-service rule of R4 (/api/recovery/<short>/v1) has no <short> for the platform library.
evidence: Ownership Map sheet Endpoints: GET /feature-flags PLT; GET /admin/feature-flags PLT; POST /admin/feature-flags PLT; PATCH /admin/feature-flags/{flagKey} PLT; POST /admin/workflows/smoke PLT. API Specification v4 gives those five operations x-module P2 (feature flags) and x-module P3 (smoke). Arch v5 slide 41 lists 19 services and no platform service; slide 34 puts gateway-bff outside the 19.
proposed: Confirm that the platform-owned operations are published on the edge surface (gateway-bff document) and state their base path, or give the platform library its own contract document and path outside the 19 service bases.

title: Event payload property types, formats and required flags are not specified in any source
source: Recovery Workbench Event and Messaging Design v4; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: Event and Messaging Design v4 sheet Events, column Payload; Arch v5 slides 42 and 43 (event catalogue) and slide 35 (Kafka line)
description: The payload column of Event and Messaging Design v4 gives the field names of each event and nothing else (for example EV-01 CaseCreated: 'caseId, caseNo, productGroup, accounts, businessDate'); it states no JSON type, format, nullability or required flag for any field, and no nested object shape for the composite fields (accounts, terms, fields, result, documents). The Arch v5 event catalogue gives the event name, the producer, the topic and the consumers only, with the note that schemas are versioned in the registry with BACKWARD compatibility. The AsyncAPI 3.0 documents of v5 therefore carry the field names as property names with no type, and the gap is recorded rather than a type invented.
evidence: Event and Messaging Design v4 sheet Events rows EV-01 to EV-30, column Payload: field names only. Arch v5 slide 42 notes: 'Schemas are versioned in the registry with BACKWARD compatibility; the AsyncAPI document per service is the contract' and gives no field type. Arch v5 slide 35: JSON Schema registry with BACKWARD compatibility. No source in the read list gives an event JSON Schema.
proposed: Publish the JSON Schema of each event payload in the registry and copy it into the AsyncAPI documents, or confirm that field names only are the agreed contract for the first release so that each producer owns its schema types in its CON story.

title: No event is catalogued for rwb-reporting, and two catalogue rows give no topic
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: Slide 41 (service catalogue, topic column); slides 42 and 43 (event catalogue, rows 01 to 30 and the carry-on rows)
description: Two holes in the event catalogue meet in the AsyncAPI set. (1) Slide 41 gives rwb-reporting the topic rwb.reporting.events.v1, but no row of slide 42 or 43 names rwb-reporting as a producer, so its AsyncAPI document has a topic and no channel. (2) Slide 43 carries the row 'TreatmentClosed, GuaranteeClaim* | rwb-treatment / guarantee | - | rwb-case, rwb-reporting': the topic cell is a dash for two producers in one row and the event name of the second is a wildcard, so neither the topic nor the exact event names of the guarantee claims are stated.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 41 row P9: rwb-reporting, topic rwb.reporting.events.v1. Slide 42 rows 01 to 19: no rwb-reporting producer. Slide 43 rows 20 to 30: no rwb-reporting producer. Slide 43 carry-on row: 'TreatmentClosed, GuaranteeClaim* | rwb-treatment / guarantee | - | rwb-case, rwb-reporting'.
proposed: Name the events that rwb-reporting publishes on rwb.reporting.events.v1, or retire the topic; name the guarantee-claim events that rwb-guarantee publishes on rwb.guarantee.events.v1 and confirm the topic of TreatmentClosed.

title: Seven component schemas of API Specification v4 are referenced by no operation
description: The v4 document defines 172 component schemas. Reachable from the 141 operations are 165: the operations carry 148 direct $ref values, and the closure over responses adds the rest. DocumentVersion, FieldCaptureItem, FieldCaptureManifest, Listing, PlacementResult, QueueOwnerLoad and WriteOff are referenced by no operation and by no other schema, so a split by operation drops them unless they are placed deliberately. The v5 set keeps them, in the document of the service that owns the domain, because rule 1 forbids losing a section of the source; the author of each may want to retire them.
evidence: Parsed v4 components.schemas: 172 entries. Closure of the $ref graph from the 141 operations: 174 nodes (165 schemas, 9 responses). Absent from the closure: DocumentVersion, FieldCaptureItem, FieldCaptureManifest, Listing, PlacementResult, QueueOwnerLoad, WriteOff.
proposed: Confirm that the seven schemas are retired in the first release of the registry, or name the operation that should return each of them.
